Map of the community }} }} [[File:The quarry, Llanwddyn NLW3361910.jpg|thumb|The Quarry, Llanwddyn]] '''Llanwddyn''' ({{Audio|Cy-Llanwddyn.ogg|Welsh pronunciation}}) is a village and [[Community (Wales)|community]] in [[Montgomeryshire]], [[Powys]], [[Wales]]. The community is centred on the [[Lake Vyrnwy]] reservoir. The original Llanwddyn village, about {{convert|2|mi|km}} northwest, was submerged when the reservoir was created in the 1880s. ==Geography== Llanwddyn borders the county of [[Gwynedd]] to the northeast, with the Powys communities of [[Llangynog]] and [[Pen-y-Bont-Fawr]] to the northwest, [[Llanfihangel-yng-Ngwynfa]] to the south east and [[Banwy]] to the southwest.[https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/election-maps/gb/ Election Maps], [[Ordnance Survey]]. Retrieved 31 January 2018. The community is sparsely populated, but includes the village of [[Abertridwr, Powys|Abertridwr]] as well as the new village of Llanwddyn. According to the [[United Kingdom Census 2011|2011 census]] the community had 99 occupied households and a population of 257, with only 84 of the residents born in Wales.{{NOMIS2011|id=1170221605|title=Llanwddyn Parish|access-date=18 February 2018}} This is a 17% decrease since the 310 people noted in [[United Kingdom Census 2001|2001]].{{cite web|title=Area: Llanwddyn (Parish) |url=http://www.neighbourhood.statistics.gov.uk/dissemination/LeadTableView.do?a=7&b=11125993&c=Llanwddyn&d=16&e=16&g=6491126&i=1001x1003x1032x1004&o=362&m=0&r=1&s=1439281225996&enc=1&dsFamilyId=789 |publisher=[[Office for National Statistics]] |date=18 November 2004 |access-date=11 August 2015}} In 2011, only 38% of the population could speak [[Welsh language|Welsh]], a decline from 60% in 2001.{{cite web |title=2011 Census results by Community |url=http://www.comisiynyddygymraeg.cymru/English/Assistance/Dataandstatisitcs/Pages/2011CensusresultsbyCommunity.aspx |publisher=[[Welsh Language Commissioner]] |year=2015 |access-date=11 August 2015 }}{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ===Lake Vyrnwy=== {{main|Lake Vyrnwy}} The main feature of the community is the {{convert|4.54|km2}} reservoir, which drowned the original village when it was created in the 1880s. [[File:Building the dam, Llanwddyn NLW3361924.jpg|thumb|left|Llanwddyn Dam c.1885 under construction]] ===Climate=== {{Weather box |location = Lake Vyrnwy No 2 (360m elevation) 1981–2010 |collapsed = |metric first = y |single line = y |Jan high C = 5.5 |Feb high C = 5.5 |Mar high C = 7.6 |Apr high C = 10.2 |May high C = 13.5 |Jun high C = 16.0 |Jul high C = 17.9 |Aug high C = 17.5 |Sep high C = 15.1 |Oct high C = 11.5 |Nov high C = 8.2 |Dec high C = 5.9 |year high C = 11.2 |Jan low C = 1.0 |Feb low C = 0.6 |Mar low C = 2.1 |Apr low C = 3.3 |May low C = 6.1 |Jun low C = 8.7 |Jul low C = 10.8 |Aug low C = 10.7 |Sep low C = 9.0 |Oct low C = 6.4 |Nov low C = 3.6 |Dec low C = 1.4 |year low C = 5.3 |Jan rain mm = 193.1 |Feb rain mm = 143.3 |Mar rain mm = 138.6 |Apr rain mm = 96.4 |May rain mm = 92.5 |Jun rain mm = 90.6 |Jul rain mm = 96.2 |Aug rain mm = 94.2 |Sep rain mm = 115.8 |Oct rain mm = 199.9 |Nov rain mm = 176.2 |Dec rain mm = 198.6 |year rain mm = 1635.4 |unit rain days= 1.0 mm |Jan rain days = 18.0 |Feb rain days = 14.0 |Mar rain days = 16.6 |Apr rain days = 13.0 |May rain days = 13.3 |Jun rain days = 12.3 |Jul rain days = 12.7 |Aug rain days = 13.8 |Sep rain days = 13.2 |Oct rain days = 18.4 |Nov rain days = 17.4 |Dec rain days = 18.8 |year rain days = 181.5 |source 1 = metoffice.gov.uk{{cite web | url=https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/climate/maps-and-data/uk-climate-averages/gcms1hjef | title=Climate Normals 1981–2010 | publisher=Met Office | access-date=24 February 2021}} | date=24 February 2021 }} ==History== [[File:St Wddyn's church, Llanwddyn - geograph.org.uk - 2471169.jpg|thumb|240px|St Wddyn's Church, dating from 1888]] By the mid-19th century the village of Llanwddyn consisted of thirty seven houses, a church and two chapels, three pubs and several shops.{{cite web|url=http://www.abandonedcommunities.co.uk/page32.html |title=Abandoned Communities... Reservoirs of Wales |publisher=AbandonedCommunities.co.uk|page=32|access-date=31 January 2018}} The population of the parish had dropped from 668 in 1831 to 443 in 1871.{{cite web|url=http://www.lake-vyrnwy.com/history.html |title=History of Lake Vyrnwy: The Valley in the Days Before the Lake |publisher=Lake Vyrnwy Tourism|year=2014|access-date=31 January 2018}} In 1873 the local vicar, Reverend Thomas H. Evans, published a mass of information about Llanwddyn in Volume VI of the ''Montgomeryshire Collections''. He described the abundance of water with, for example, one third of the valley being regularly under water during the winter. In 1877 the expanding English city of [[Liverpool]] identified the Vyrnwy Valley as a suitable site for a reservoir to supply fresh water to its citizens. A parliamentary bill was drawn up to authorise the construction of a dam and reservoir. The population of Llanwddyn were not consulted, though they presented a signed petition against the proposals. The [[Liverpool Corporation Waterworks]] Act was passed in 1880 and construction of a dam across the valley began in 1881. It took seven years to complete. The old village was demolished, the valley flooded, and the water reached the lip of the dam on 22 November 1889. [[File:Llyn Llanwddyn - Vyrnwy Dam, Powys, Wales built over a village to supply water to Liverpool 04.jpg|thumb|240px|Lake Vyrnwy Hotel, Llanwddyn]] A new village was constructed below the dam to house the original residents. It included a church, dedicated to St Wddyn, which was consecrated on 27 November 1888, the day before the valve of the dam was finally closed. A [[Hydroelectricity|hydroelectric]] power plant was built for the village in 1902. The reservoir brought jobs and relative prosperity to the community, with the population remaining relatively stable for the next 70 years. In 1974, ownership of the estate passed from the Liverpool Corporation to the [[Severn Trent|Severn Trent Water Authority]] . ==Governance== Llanwddyn has a [[community council]] which has up to seven locally elected councillors.{{cite web |url=http://www.llanwddyncc.co.uk/ |title=Llanwddyn Community Council |publisher=Llanwddyn Community Council |access-date=31 January 2018}} Llanwddyn also gives its name to the [[Llanwddyn (electoral ward)|Llanwddyn]] [[electoral ward]] which elects a councillor to [[Powys County Council]]. At the [[Powys County Council election, 2017|May 2017 council election]] Bryn Davies won Llanwddyn as [[Plaid Cymru]]'s first seat on Powys Council.{{cite news|author=Keri Trigg |url=http://www.rhyljournal.co.uk/news/15839448.A_mix_of_old_and_new_councillors_win_seats_in_Montgomeryshire_in_Powys_County_Council_elections/ |title=A mix of old and new councillors win seats in Montgomeryshire in Powys County Council elections |work=Rhyl, Prestatyn & Abergele Journal |date=5 May 2017 |access-date=28 January 2018}} == Cultural references == The flooding of Llanwddyn is referenced in [[W. G. Sebald|W.G. Sebald's]] 2001 novel [[Austerlitz (novel)|Austerlitz]]; the titular character is disturbed and affected by his imagining of the drowned village after being shown the Vyrnwy reservoir by his adoptive father, who was born there. {{cite book |last1=Sebald |first1=W.G. |title=Austerlitz |date=2001 |publisher=Modern Library |isbn=978-0-679-64541-2}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.llanwddyncc.co.uk/ Llanwddyn Community Council] {{Commons category|Llanwddyn}} {{Powys}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Llanwddyn| ]] [[Category:Former villages in Wales]] [[Category:Forcibly depopulated communities in Wales]]
